variants.name: Named type with typed constants
variants.idiom_name: named type + typed const block (+ String() via stringer)
variants.implementation_notes: Go has no enum keyword, and untyped constants convert implicitly, so the idiom is a named type plus a const block: the named type stops values of two different sets from mixing, and string-backed constants serialize readably. It does not close the set - Suit(3) and untyped literals still compile - so the zero value is reserved as an explicit sentinel, parsing goes through a validating function, and String() is generated with stringer rather than hand-written.
pitfalls: The named type is not a closed set: Suit(3) and untyped integer literals are assignable, so validate at every boundary.
iota-based values shift when members are inserted or reordered; pin explicit values whenever they are persisted or sent over the wire.
The zero value is a real member unless skipped (`_ = iota`); always define an explicit unknown/invalid sentinel.

variants.name: Struct-based enum with unexported field
variants.idiom_name: struct with unexported field + package-level instances + FromX parser
variants.implementation_notes: When invalid values must be unrepresentable in memory, replace the primitive-typed constant with a struct whose only field is unexported: code outside the package cannot construct a value, so the package-level instances are the entire value set. The cost is that instances are variables, not constants (they can be reassigned and are not protected), and the zero value is the empty struct, which must be treated as invalid. Add a FromString constructor that validates and a String() method for formatting.
pitfalls: Struct instances are package-level variables: another part of the same package can overwrite them, and nothing is enforced across packages only because the field is unexported.
The zero value Suit{} is always constructible and comparable to valid values - treat it as the invalid sentinel.
Structs are not constants, so they cannot be used in constant expressions (array sizes, case labels, const declarations).
